title: Rollouts: Console release notes + model change history (wireframes + interaction details)
creator: Kenji Nakamura
project: Model metadata schema v1 + automated changelog (Console + docs)
description:
## Why
Customers (and Support) currently struggle to answer “what changed, when did it change for me, and how do I roll back?” during model promotions and rollouts. This ticket produces the wireframes + interaction details needed for engineering to implement:
- Per-model change history (release notes timeline)
- Console-wide release notes feed (workspace scoped)
- In-rollout “What’s changing?” panel + full notes drawer

This is the design companion to:
- Confluence UX spec: Console UX Spec: Model Change History & Release Notes (Rollouts/A-B)
- Editorial rules: Customer Release Notes Taxonomy & Style Guide

## Deliverables (what’s in Figma)
1) Model Details → History tab
- Filters row (time range / deployment mode / region / category / “Affected my workspace” toggle)
- Timeline list using a “Release note entry card” component
- Expand/collapse behavior (card expands to structured sections)
- Status pills + “Effective in” scope chips
- Empty states + partial empty states
- Error state when release notes backend is unavailable

2) Console-wide Release notes feed
- Same card component, with model name + deep link
- Default toggle ON: “Affected my workspace”
- Pagination variant (stable URLs) and infinite scroll option (not recommended, but shown for discussion)

3) Rollouts: embedded “What’s changing?” panel + drawer
- Rollout create flow (candidate selection step): show release note summary for the candidate version/profile
- Rollout detail page (active rollout): persistent panel with baseline vs candidate
- “View full release notes” opens drawer with same expanded sections + rollout-scope callout (regions/cohorts/split)

4) RBAC and redaction UX
- Internal roles see a “Show internal details” toggle (OFF by default)
- When enabled: internal-only section appears with distinct styling + persistent “Do not share externally” banner
- Customer roles never see the toggle (server-side enforced; UI assumes defense-in-depth)

## Key interaction details (engineering-facing)
### Release note entry card (component behavior)
Collapsed state shows:
- Category badge + Severity (Low/Medium/High)
- Title (truncate w/ tooltip)
- Timestamp (localized)
- “Effective in” scope (chips, +N more)
- Summary (2–4 lines, truncate w/ Read more)
- “From → To” version line (if applicable)
- Footer links (only if present): Migration/compatibility notes, Rollback guidance, Known limitations
- Status pill (Available / Rolling out / Scheduled / Reverted)

Expanded state reveals:
- What changed
- Who is affected
- Required action (or “No action required”)
- Rollback / mitigation
- Deprecation timeline (if present)
- Quality notes (bounded language; no hard claims without evidence)

Internal-only (behind toggle + RBAC):
- Related events list (event IDs + timestamps)
- Actor/source (registry vs control plane)
- Link-out to audit log query (internal)

### Filters and scope logic (UI expectations)
- Deployment mode filter only shows modes the workspace is entitled to.
- Region filter disables invalid combinations (e.g., Dedicated region not available).
- “Affected my workspace” toggle:
  - Default ON in global Release notes feed
  - Default OFF in per-model History tab (to allow broader browsing), but we show a tooltip explaining the difference
- If filters yield zero results:
  - Show a friendly empty state with actions (expand time range, remove region filter, go to global feed)
- If some regions have results and others don’t:
  - Keep list, show a small “No changes found for X regions” hint under filters (no blocking empty state)

### Rollouts panel nuances
- Canary: emphasize “Expected impact window” (if schedule exists) and show rollback guidance prominently.
- A/B: show baseline vs candidate context; optional “Quality signals available” callout (no metrics in v1 UI, link-out only if customer-safe).

### Responsive behavior
- Wide: filters in one row, cards full width, optional right-rail (History tab only).
- Narrow: filters wrap into 2–3 rows; Rollouts panel becomes a top section; drawer becomes full-screen modal.

### Accessibility requirements (called out in mocks)
- Keyboard navigation for all filters and card expansion.
- Badge colors not sole indicator; include text labels.
- Screen-reader friendly “Effective in” chip expansion.
- Long model/version strings wrap (no horizontal scrolling in cards).

## Content constraints (alignment w/ style guide)
- Title <= 80 chars recommended
- Summary <= 280 chars recommended
- Avoid: incident references, Jira/Slack links, customer names, internal service names (unless already public)
- Performance claims must be metric + conditions (but UI should not encourage stuffing metrics into title)

## Open questions to resolve in review
1) IA placement: Left nav “Release notes” under Models vs Observability vs Operations.
2) Pagination vs infinite scroll: recommendation is pagination for stable URLs and shareability.
3) Private offline: do we show “Installed bundle version” in History for connected Private only, and “Last exported notes” for offline? (Mocks show both states.)
4) “Rolling out” without ETA: copy treatment (“No ETA”) and whether to show partial rollout progress bar (not in v1).
5) “Customer-safe link” for Support: potential future enhancement (not in mocks), but requested by Support for screen-sharing.

## Acceptance criteria
- Figma contains annotated flows for all three surfaces (History tab, global feed, Rollouts panel + drawer).
- Component spec for release note card and filters is included (states + empty/error).
- RBAC/internal toggle behavior is explicitly documented in annotations.
- Copy blocks for empty/error states are included (final-ish, not lorem ipsum).
- Engineering handoff notes include expected API fields (high-level) and loading skeleton behavior.

## Handoff notes / assets
- Uses existing Console design system primitives where possible; new components: Status pill variants + “Effective in” chip list pattern.
- Loading: skeleton cards (3) + shimmer line for summary.
- Error: inline banner with Retry, non-blocking (rollout controls remain usable).

comments: 2025-10-06 — Kenji Nakamura: Kicked off initial wireframes based on the UX spec. Focus for M1 is History tab + Rollouts “What’s changing?” panel. Global feed will be included but may be slightly lower fidelity pending IA decision.

2025-10-08 — Marissa Cole: Please make “Affected my workspace” the default on the global feed and very obvious when it’s OFF (we’ve had customers misinterpret “available to workspace” as “happened to me”). Also ensure the per-model History tab can be switched to “Affected my workspace” without losing other filters.

2025-10-09 — Chloe Martin: For backend feasibility: please annotate which fields are required on the card vs only in expanded state. We want to keep list endpoint payload small; can fetch full body on expand/drawer open.

2025-10-10 — Nora Ahmed: Support needs a consistent way to confirm what customers can see. Can we add an internal-only “Copy customer-safe summary” action? If not v1, please at least make sure internal toggle is visually loud to avoid screen-share leaks.

2025-10-11 — Kenji Nakamura: Updated mocks: internal toggle is OFF by default, does not persist by default, and shows a persistent banner when ON. Added annotations for list payload vs details payload. Added empty/error states copy.

2025-10-14 — Paula Mendes: For rollouts panel, can we surface a short “Rollback” CTA right on the panel (not only inside drawer) when severity is High? This will help during active incidents. Also, for A/B, call out that some traffic may still be on baseline during analysis (avoid implying full cutover).

2025-10-15 — Tessa Morgan: Visual: status pill + category badge stacking felt noisy in the card header. Recommend: keep category badge left, status pill right, severity as a small text label under category (not another pill). Also please confirm contrast on badge colors meets AA.

2025-10-17 — Dylan Brooks: +1 on pagination for stable URLs. Also, add a note for engineering: do not silently drop invalid filter combos; disable and explain. We’ve been burned by hidden filter coercion.

2025-10-18 — Kenji Nakamura: Addressed review: reduced header chrome, adjusted status/severity layout, added a11y notes on contrast + non-color indicators. Added “Rollback” CTA to rollouts panel for High severity entries (links to guidance, not an action). Marking In Review for final sign-off.

2025-10-20 — Naomi Feldman: Please ensure security-sensitive copy guidance is referenced in annotations (no CVE details, no internal incident references). If we ever render Security category, it must go through Security review gate; the UI should not suggest otherwise. Looks good to proceed.
